acceptanceCriteria: The full declared workspace verification requirement remains enforced and is represented by one or more explicit Runtime verification nodes without silently dropping packages, targets, or test classes.

Every verification node has an identity-bound receipt containing command identity, repository snapshot, Runtime identity, exit status, bounded logs, elapsed time, and timeout state; a lost or unknown exit status cannot become a pass.

The execution boundary distinguishes per-node timeout from plan timeout, terminates descendants, leaves no test subprocess or lock leak, and records a structured failure when a node times out or is interrupted.
A successful bounded plan is accepted by the normal Work Item lifecycle as formal verification evidence and can proceed to finish without hand-written or imported substitute receipts.
Recovery reuses only complete, identity-matching node evidence; an interrupted or partial plan reruns only missing or invalid nodes and preserves prior evidence.
Focused regressions cover node splitting or aggregation, timeout and interruption, exit-code and log persistence, descendant cleanup, stale or foreign receipts, and CLI/MCP parity.
The documented command surface explains the supported long-running verification route without instructing Agents to bypass the Runtime.
goal: Replace the single-node verification bottleneck with an identity-bound fail-closed execution boundary that preserves the full workspace test requirement while allowing bounded nodes and reliable evidence capture.
intent: Make long-running repository verification complete through the Runtime without losing exit status, logs, child-process cleanup, or formal verification receipt.
outOfScope: WI-819 documentation-gate fixes and its Contract
weakening or lowering workspace test requirements
arbitrary external evidence as a substitute for local verification
requiredEvidenceClasses: full workspace coverage manifest and deterministic node plan
successful formal verification receipt bound to WI-820
timeout and interruption regression receipts with no leaked descendants
before/after elapsed time and process-count measurements

scenarioCoverage.expected: The declared cargo test --locked --workspace requirement is represented by a deterministic set of Runtime nodes with no package, target, or test-class omission.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Compare the node manifest and aggregate command coverage with Cargo workspace metadata and run the bounded plan in the same repository snapshot.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A node timeout or interruption records a structured failure, preserves bounded output, terminates descendants, and leaves no test process or lock behind.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the controlled timeout and descendant fixtures, inspect the receipt fields, and check process and lock state after termination.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A successful bounded verification plan is recorded as current identity-bound Work Item verification evidence; unknown exit status or direct cargo output cannot pass as a receipt.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise the CLI lifecycle with a successful bounded plan, a failed command, and an unavailable exit status, then validate the persisted receipt bindings.

scenarioCoverage.expected: An interrupted plan reruns only missing or stale nodes and reuses complete identity-matching node evidence without rewriting prior evidence.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Provide a mixed receipt store containing fresh, stale, foreign, and missing node results and assert the planned execution and persisted recovery evidence.
